title: The State of AI in 2026: On the Road to ROI
content: McKinsey's annual State of AI survey. AI adoption keeps rising (nearly nine in ten organizations use it) but financial payoff lags, with only about six percent seeing significant profit impact. High performers differ by redesigning workflows around AI rather than bolting it onto old processes.

title: Mistral Agents API
content: Mistral's API for building enterprise AI agents. Offers built-in connectors (code execution, image generation, document library for RAG, web search), MCP tool support, persistent memory, and multi-agent orchestration with hand-offs. Adding web search sharply raised factual accuracy in their benchmark.

title: Mistral launches Le Chat Enterprise with Medium 3
content: Mistral's enterprise push: Le Chat Enterprise powered by the Medium 3 model, with hybrid and on-premises deployment, data sovereignty, and strict access controls aimed at regulated industries.

title: Measuring Agent Autonomy
content: Anthropic research on how to measure how autonomous AI agents are, and the deployment overhang: the gap between what models are capable of and the narrower autonomy they are actually trusted to exercise in practice.

title: Change-Intelligent Stakeholder Engagement
content: A project-management guide to stakeholder engagement that extends the power/interest grid with an attitude dimension and gives tactics for handling resistant or high-power stakeholders during change initiatives.

title: You're Not Ready for AI Agents Unless You Can Answer These 10 Questions
content: Ten questions leaders should answer before deploying AI agents, covering autonomy level, ownership, failure handling, and organizational readiness, framed as a go/no-go checklist.

title: Three Roles That Shape Discovery and Engagement in Enterprise AI Adoption
content: Describes the three roles that shape discovery and engagement during enterprise AI adoption and how each influences whether a deployment succeeds.

title: Six Stages of Deploying Enterprise AI (and Where Most Teams Go Wrong)
content: A deployment-process playbook walking the six stages of rolling out enterprise AI, from discovery through adoption and oversight, and where most teams go wrong at each stage.

title: The Trust Ladder: Why AI Adoption Should Be Earned
content: Argues AI adoption should be earned rung by rung, from suggestion to instruction to delegation, with each level requiring evidence of reliability before the system is granted more autonomy.

title: Are AI Agents Rewriting the Consumer Adoption Curve?
content: Asks whether AI agents change the usual adoption curve, and argues that permission and trust metrics reveal the truth where usage and awareness metrics flatter.

title: Agentic AI Adoption: Closing the Daily-Use Gap
content: On closing the gap between AI adoption and real daily use, distinguishing breadth, depth (tasks completed per active user), and repeat usage rather than treating adoption as one number.

title: How to Measure AI Adoption Without Vanity Metrics
content: How to measure AI adoption without vanity metrics, moving beyond logins and prompt counts toward signals of real value and earned trust.

title: Measuring AI That Acts: Adoption Is a Trust Ladder, Not a Login Count
content: Reframes adoption for AI that takes actions as a trust ladder rather than a login count. Proposes autonomy share and override rate as the honest metrics, with each metric tied to a decision it should drive.

title: A Comprehensive Guide to Stakeholder Analysis in AI Governance (Part 2)
content: A guide to stakeholder analysis in AI governance: identifying and engaging the parties whose buy-in and oversight an AI system needs across its lifecycle.

title: How I Learned to Stop Trusting My AI Pipeline and Actually Measure It
content: A learning-journey piece on building an LLM evaluation framework for a KPI summarization pipeline, and why deployed AI output must be measured, not trusted.

title: Agent Memory: Start Designing What Deserves to Be Remembered
content: An analytics-led take on designing memory for AI agents: short-term vs long-term, what deserves to be remembered, and why the hard part is deciding what to store, not storage itself.

title: Building Effective Agents
content: Anthropic's guide to building effective agents. Favors simple, composable patterns over heavy frameworks, distinguishes workflows from agents, and advises adding complexity only when it clearly earns its keep.

title: The Ultimate Guide to Chunking Strategies for RAG Applications
content: A Databricks guide to chunking strategies for RAG with code examples: fixed-size, semantic, and recursive chunking, how chunks are embedded and stored in Vector Search, and how chunk size and overlap affect retrieval quality.

title: Chunking Strategies for RAG
content: An explainer of RAG chunking strategies: fixed-size, sentence-based, recursive, semantic, and late chunking, and the core tradeoff that chunks too large hide passages while chunks too small lose context.

title: Mosaic AI Vector Search (documentation)
content: Databricks documentation for Mosaic AI Vector Search (AI Search): creating an endpoint and a Delta Sync index, embedding model options, primary keys, and querying the index.

title: Announcing Hybrid Search GA in Mosaic AI Vector Search
content: Announcement of hybrid search general availability in Mosaic AI Vector Search, combining keyword and vector retrieval to improve result quality over vector-only search.

title: Building Effective Agents (annotated notes)
content: Annotated notes on Anthropic's Building Effective Agents, highlighting the workflow-versus-agent distinction and practical takeaways for keeping agent designs simple.

title: Enterprise AI Adoption & Change-Management Playbook
content: A change-management playbook for driving real adoption of AI that acts on a user's behalf, framing adoption as autonomy earned rung by rung on a trust ladder rather than as usage. Covers the five sources of resistance and the lever for each, honest adoption metrics (acceptance/override, consolidation, guardrails), staged rollout and anti-patterns, and a one-page adoption plan.
